The search didn't turn up a dedicated Houston 311 service requests page on data.houstontx.gov. The 311 data I found is hosted on the City's GIS server, and the one data.houstontx.gov result is unrelated.

- **Archived cases:** A GIS layer of Houston 311 requests runs from 2011 to April 2024, with its last update in April 2024. It holds all publicly available requests from the LAGAN system, excluding animal-related (BARC) tickets, which are in a separate system. The layer is meant to be used alongside a separate BARC location dataset. "Houston 311 Service Requests (2011/11/10 - 2024/04/16)" is its description, and it is hosted at mycity2.houstontx.gov.
- **Recent requests:** A separate layer covers open cases and cases closed within the past two weeks, refreshed every 30 minutes, per its service description.
- **Mirrored copies:** ArcGIS FeatureServer copies of 311 datasets (for example, flood-event subsets) appear on services.arcgis.com with the same LAGAN-based description.
- **data.houstontx.gov:** The only hit from that domain is a page on the top 5 public information requests per department, which is a different topic.
- **Context:** A February 2025 city presentation says Houston 311 creates about 400,000 service requests a year, and that departments, not 311, close them.

I couldn't confirm whether the monthly archive has been updated since April 2024, so check the GIS service page directly before relying on it. A search of data.houstontx.gov for "311" might also surface a current export.

The City of Philadelphia's 311 dataset records Philly311 requests from late 2014 onward. It covers requests made through the 311 app, phone, in person, email, the website, and social media. The dataset includes two main data points: requests for services or information. A service request represents a need that the City government would fulfill, like getting a pothole fixed.

Because the file is large, the city suggests a different approach for non-API users. Unless you are comfortable working with APIs, the city recommends using the visualization to explore the data. Those who use the API can query it through Carto. If full CSV or SHP downloads fail, the dataset is split up by year, and you need to download every year to see the full dataset. Data.gov lists yearly CSV and SHP files covering 2014 through 2025.

Other details from the listings: the dataset is updated daily under a City of Philadelphia license, and the maintainer contact is 311datarequest@phila.gov. Data.gov shows a metadata update dated April 13, 2026.

Note that these are mostly catalog and metadata pages, not the live data, so check the OpenDataPhilly page for current file links and the license terms.

Each city has a 311 dataset on its official portal. Houston's isn't on its CKAN portal, and LA's is split into one dataset per year.

| City | Dataset URL | Platform | Update frequency as stated | Earliest year | Closure field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **NYC** | https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/erm2-nwe9 ("311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present") | Socrata | "Updated daily" | 2020 in this dataset. 2010 in the companion archive https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/76ig-c548 (2010–2019) | `closed_date` |
| **Los Angeles** | Current year: https://data.lacity.org/d/2cy6-i7zn ("MyLA311 Cases 2026"). Earliest year I found: https://data.lacity.org/d/ndkd-k878 (2016) | Socrata | "Daily" (refresh-rate metadata field) | 2016 | `closeddate` |
| **Chicago** | https://data.cityofchicago.org/d/v6vf-nfxy ("311 Service Requests") | Socrata | "Data are updated multiple times per day" | The new system launched 12/18/2018, with some legacy records flagged in `LEGACY_RECORD` | `closed_date` |
| **Houston** | https://311.houstontx.gov/servicerequestdata.html (yearly pipe-delimited files at hfdapp.houstontx.gov/311/) | Other: city-hosted flat files, not on the CKAN portal at data.houstontx.gov | Month-to-date and year-to-date files daily. Past 3 years weekly. Older data "static". | 2011 | `Closed Date` |
| **Philadelphia** | https://opendataphilly.org/datasets/311-service-and-information-requests/ (Carto table `public_cases_fc`) | Other: CARTO, catalogued on OpenDataPhilly (CKAN-style) | "Updated daily" | 2014 (since Dec 8, 2014) | `closed_datetime` |
| **San Francisco** | https://data.sf.gov/d/vw6y-z8j6 ("311 Cases") | Socrata | "Publishing frequency: Daily". Data change frequency is "Multiple times per hour". The description says "updates nightly". | 2008 (cases since 7/1/2008) | `closed_date` |

Caveats:
- **LA:** The years 2016–2026 are separate datasets (for example, 2017 is `eq98-9f8w`, 2024 is `b7dx-7gc3`, and 2025 is `h73f-gn57`). I only read part of the portal's catalog listing, so there may be an older MyLA311 year that I missed. The 2016 dataset is the earliest I confirmed.
- **Houston:** The ArcGIS archive layer (`311_ARCHIVED_CASES`, 2011–April 2024) and its recent-requests layer were returning 500 "service not started" errors. I took the closure field from the header of the 2026 year-to-date file. The 311 page itself gives no column descriptions.
- **Philadelphia:** I got the field name from a live query against the Carto API. The OpenDataPhilly page doesn't list fields.
- **SF:** `updated_datetime` also holds the closure date for closed requests, but `closed_date` is the dedicated field.
